question: A student watches a chat model pause for a second and then produce its answer a word or two at a time. She concludes her internet connection is slow. What is the better explanation?

options.text: The full answer was finished before anything appeared and is shown gradually to feel conversational
options.feedback: There is no finished answer waiting. Each fragment appears only when a fresh run of the model has produced it, so the trickle reflects real work happening.

options.text: Each piece of text is the model completing a full run and producing one more token
options.feedback: The pause and the trickle are the model itself running, once per token. Every visible fragment means the whole pipeline just executed again on a slightly longer context.

options.text: The server is holding her request in a queue behind other users
options.feedback: Queuing can add delay before the first word, but it does not explain the steady word-by-word arrival afterward. That rhythm is the model generating one token per run.

options.text: Her browser is rendering the text more slowly than it received it
options.feedback: Browsers render text far faster than it arrives here. The pacing is set upstream, by how long each run of the model takes to produce the next token.
